a supersymmetric theory with a low-energy supersymmetry breaking scale can be tested by experiments that measure the electron and the neutron electric dipole moments.

the electric dipole moments of both the electron and the neutron can be used as probes of supersymmetry and its breaking, and of the unification of the gauge couplings, in the same way that the muon anomalous magnetic moment has been used so far.
